description: 🚀 Artemis III is a team of passionate developers, space enthusiasts, and creative builders.
summary: Elysion is a phone-first space mission design game. Players choose a destination, a rocket, a spacecraft and science instruments. The game checks the design against real constraints (mass, power, delta-v and communication) and explains in plain language why it works or fails. Then it launches the mission into Mission Control. A built-in Solar System view shows the mission on real orbits. Every planet, 177 moons and 10 dwarf planets are placed from NASA/JPL data for any date, with real launch windows, eclipses and conjunctions computed on the fly. A one-tap sample mission takes a first-time player from opening the app to launch in under a minute, and every mission ends with a NASA-fact debrief. It runs in any phone browser with no account and no install. Data sources are credited in the app, simplified game models are labelled, and over 590 automated checks cover the physics and data.
details:
What it is

Elysion: Beyond Earth is our entry for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. Players design a space mission, then watch it fly on an accurate, live model of the Solar System.

How it works

  • Build: choose a destination, objective, rocket, spacecraft and science instruments.
  • Validate: the game checks mass, power, delta-v (Tsiolkovsky rocket equation), communication, science score and risk.
  • Learn: when a design fails, the “Why?” button explains the cause in plain words, so players know what to change.
  • Fly: valid missions launch into Mission Control and play out on a live Solar System.

A computed sky, not a picture

  • Planet positions use NASA/JPL approximate planetary elements.
  • Moon orbits use JPL Planetary Satellite Mean Elements.
  • Dwarf-planet orbits use the JPL Small-Body Database and Observatoire de Paris data.
  • Launch windows, eclipses and conjunctions are calculated for any date.

Benefits and impact

  • Teaches real mission-design trade-offs to students and the public.
  • Runs in a phone browser with no install, account or trackers.
  • Built to WCAG 2.1 AA, with a strict Content-Security-Policy.

What makes it creative

  • A game that explains itself: every failure comes with a plain-language reason.
  • A one-tap sample mission that gets a new player to launch in under a minute.
  • A NASA-fact debrief quiz after every mission.
  • Generative music produced in the browser.

Tools and technology

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP (static hosting) and Python (data tools), with Node and Playwright for testing. More than 590 automated checks cover the physics and data.

Honest about limits

Simplified models are labelled GAME MODEL, and approximate positions are marked ≈ in the app.
